strokeOrderSource.citation: Zer o Zabar, Be, kāf, and short vowels, independent ب handwriting animation and Be instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The independent-form handwriting animation draws the full be-series bowl first in one uninterrupted right-to-left run, then places the single dot below after one lift. The adjacent prose identifies every be form as a shallow curve with one dot below and instructs writers to complete a word's right-to-left main line before returning, again right-to-left, to add dots and other marks. This learner path covers the independent form and fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback. The provenance remains Urdu-specific rather than borrowing the separate Arabic or Persian ب sources.
